items.claim: The row names the opening dated clause of MT 6:1 a superscription, which blends it with the book's byte-swept three-header superscription census, and it pairs a whole-verse pointed run of MT 6:5 with a two-word English gloss.
items.evidence: The row-opening clause spliced from its own cited verse is בִּשְׁנַת מוֹת֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ עֻזִּיָּ֔הוּ (oshb:Isa.6.1, byte tier). The attested class it belongs to is a date frame, not a header: the two-token consonantal string for that date formula stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses), the second being בִּשְׁנַת מ֖וֹת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָחָ֑ז (oshb:Isa.14.28, byte tier) - and that second site is itself a mid-verse burden-header reference rather than a verse-initial header. Isaiah's header census is exactly three vision/ben-Amots superscriptions (sweep: 3 verses), none of them at 6:1, so 'superscription' names an object the bytes at this verse do not carry; the boundary itself is not in dispute. Everything else in the row's Hebrew re-collates correctly: קָד֧וֹשׁ קָד֛וֹשׁ קָד֖וֹשׁ (oshb:Isa.6.3, byte tier) is rightly held as its own object and not folded into the Holy-One-of-Israel title census, and אֽוֹי (oshb:Isa.6.5, byte tier) is rightly kept apart from the verse-initial woe-onset lexeme of the preceding chapter. Secondary defects: the whole-verse pointed run of MT 6:5 is matched only to the two English words 'Woe is me!', so quote-and-gloss parity is not held; and the span is coextensive with the chapter division while carrying the top confidence band. Disclosure objects verified: the petuchah at MT 6:13 is the sole parashah mark inside the span (1 mark over MT 6:1-6:13) and it is disclosed together with the petuchah at MT 5:30 at the front seam (tier-3, single-witness); paseq segs sit at MT 6:2 and MT 6:3 (single-witness, count-only, no position claim available); no ketiv/qere note falls anywhere in MT chs 6-8, so no slicing disclosure is owed here.

items.claim: The one-unit case rests on a single embedded divine frame at MT 7:7 while three further speech onsets inside the same span go unquoted and unweighed, including a resumptive YHWH-speech frame at MT 7:10 whose defective-spelled twin four verses later is treated as a unit-cutting seam.
items.evidence: The span's own bytes carry four speech onsets, not one: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶֽל יְשַׁעְיָהוּ֒ (oshb:Isa.7.3, byte tier), כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Isa.7.7, byte tier - a divine-owned frame, correctly named as such), וַיּ֣וֹסֶף יְהוָ֔ה דַּבֵּ֥ר אֶל אָחָ֖ז לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Isa.7.10, byte tier) and וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְעוּ נָ֖א בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד (oshb:Isa.7.13, byte tier). Only the second is engaged. The MT 7:10 frame is the plene-spelled member of a plene/defective pair whose defective member, וַיֹּ֣סֶף יְהוָ֔ה דַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֛י ע֖וֹד לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Isa.8.5, byte tier), opens a separate unit further on; each spelling is a one-verse consonantal sweep (sweep: 1 verse plene; sweep: 1 verse defective), so the same resumptive-speech frame class is load-bearing at one site and silent at the other with no stated ground for the asymmetry - the row's internal frame census is incomplete exactly where its over-split reasoning needs it. Verified in the row's favour: וּשְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב (oshb:Isa.7.3, byte tier) is correctly identified as the remnant NAME site rather than the bare noun or the reactivating clauses, and the Immanu-El count-object is correctly sized (sweep: 3 verses - MT 7:14, MT 8:8, MT 8:10) with the sign's construal properly held open. Residual defects: the remnant root is described as a three-way split when the attested objects on it run wider, and the unpointed mention of the bare noun carries no tier label; the rationale also names a granularity rule by name in place of a byte argument. Parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 7:6 and MT 7:9, PE at MT 7:17 inside the span, PE at MT 6:13 at the front seam; tier-3, single-witness); no ketiv/qere note falls in this chapter.

items.claim: The four-site day-formula recurrence claim is untiered and is not one form in the bytes - three sites coincide only once accents are stripped and the fourth lacks the leading element entirely - and that same form is asked to open the row's front seam while being dismissed as non-cutting twice inside it.
items.evidence: Spliced openers: וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.7.18), וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא (oshb:Isa.7.21) and וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.7.23) each re-collate at byte tier against their own verses, but they are pairwise NOT byte-identical - the accents differ on both tokens of the formula - so they coincide only at accent-stripped tier, which the row never says. The fourth asserted site opens בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא (oshb:Isa.7.20, byte tier) without the leading element at all, so a single 'repeated formula' label is covering two distinct attested forms. Only the first of the four is quoted, leaving three asserted sites with no quoted form. No digit is supplied either: the bare day-formula string stands in 45 verses book-wide (sweep: 45 verses) and the extended form in 13 (sweep: 13 verses), so this is a book-wide device and not a structure peculiar to this unit - one of those 45 sites sits at MT 5:30, outside this chapter entirely. The seam logic is therefore non-discriminating on its own bytes: the front cut at MT 7:17|7:18 rests on a form that is accent-stripped-identical to the two internal onsets the row expressly declines to cut at, and the row gives no byte ground separating the two uses. Disclosure objects verified: parashah marks are complete and correctly typed for the span (SAMEKH at MT 7:20, PE at MT 7:25, with the front-seam PE at MT 7:17; tier-3, single-witness); one paseq seg sits at MT 7:18 (single-witness, count-only); no ketiv/qere note falls in this chapter.

items.claim: The row's front-seam driver recurs byte-for-byte inside the row's own four-verse span without cutting there, and the row discloses neither the recurrence nor any ground for the asymmetry.
items.evidence: The opener וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Isa.8.1, byte tier) recurs as וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Isa.8.3, byte tier) - the same three-token run, re-collated at byte tier against MT 8:3's own bytes, i.e. byte-identical, not merely cognate. The consonantal string for that frame stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses) and BOTH of them are inside this four-verse span. A form that occurs twice in four verses and is said to cut only at its first occurrence cannot by itself establish 'a fresh divine-command frame'; the row states the driver and never weighs its internal twin, so the front seam is carried by a non-discriminating form. The rear seam is better founded and is correctly identified: MT 8:5 opens with a materially different resumptive frame, וַיֹּ֣סֶף יְהוָ֔ה דַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֛י ע֖וֹד לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Isa.8.5, byte tier), whose consonantal spelling is a one-verse sweep (sweep: 1 verse), and the row's rival reading names it. Disclosure objects verified: the SAMEKH at MT 8:4 is the sole parashah mark inside the span (1 mark over MT 8:1-8:4) and it is disclosed with the PE at MT 7:25 at the front seam (tier-3, single-witness); a paseq seg sits at MT 8:4 (single-witness, count-only); no ketiv/qere note falls anywhere in MT chs 6-8, so nothing is owed before the row's counting or slicing language.

items.claim: The row decides a construal it simultaneously declares held - reading the closing formation of MT 8:8 as a vocative address and resting its rear-seam sentence on that reading - and it attaches a byte-tier label to an unpointed run that collates at skeleton.
items.evidence: The verse tail spliced from the cited verse is מְלֹ֥א רֹֽחַב אַרְצְךָ֖ עִמָּ֥נוּ (oshb:Isa.8.8, byte tier). The bytes there carry no vocative particle and no independent marker of address; the suffixed form אַרְצְךָ֖ (oshb:Isa.8.8, byte tier), which the English witness renders as a second-person singular possessive at web:Isa.8.8, has no antecedent named anywhere inside the verse, and the staged extract carries no morphology layer, so 'vocative address' is a form-class claim that cannot be verified from what is staged and should be held rather than asserted. The row nonetheless writes both that the site 'is read here as a vocative address' and that its relation to the earlier naming site is 'disclosed, not decided', while its rear-seam sentence runs the unit 'to its address' - so the held construal is doing boundary work. Separately, the same note attaches an explicit byte-tier label to the unpointed two-token mention of that formation; re-collated against the cited verse the unpointed run reaches skeleton tier, not byte, so a mention-grade form is carrying a quotation-grade label. Quote-and-gloss parity also fails: a multi-token pointed run of MT 8:8 is matched to the two English words 'O Immanuel'. Verified in the row's favour: the front seam is byte-sound - וַיֹּ֣סֶף יְהוָ֔ה דַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֛י ע֖וֹד לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Isa.8.5, byte tier) is a distinct resumptive frame, not the command frame of the preceding unit - and parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 8:8 inside the span, SAMEKH at MT 8:4 at the front seam; tier-3, single-witness). No ketiv/qere note falls in this chapter.

items.claim: Both seams are carried by forms actually present in the cited verses' bytes - an explicit vocative addressee at MT 8:9 and a divine-owned frame at MT 8:11 - and the row's one digit-bearing count-object is correctly named and correctly sized.
items.evidence: The row opens on רֹ֤עוּ עַמִּים֙ וָחֹ֔תּוּ (oshb:Isa.8.9, byte tier), whose addressee עַמִּים֙ (oshb:Isa.8.9, byte tier) is explicit in the bytes and is a different addressee from the second-person singular suffix that closes the preceding verse - so the addressee shift claimed for the front seam is byte-true at the claimed position. The rear seam abuts כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י (oshb:Isa.8.11, byte tier), and the frame ownership there is divine: the divine-speech-formula string stands in 48 verses book-wide (sweep: 48 verses), of which the royal-messenger sites are the four in the narrative chapters, and MT 8:11 is not among them. The Immanu-El count-object is right: the two-token consonantal string stands in exactly 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses - MT 7:14, MT 8:8, MT 8:10), so 'third and last' is sound, and the row holds the name-versus-clause relation open instead of resolving it. Its closing quote כִּ֥י עִמָּ֖נוּ אֵֽל (oshb:Isa.8.10, byte tier) re-collates at byte tier against the cited verse. Parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 8:10 inside the span, SAMEKH at MT 8:8 at the front seam; tier-3, single-witness); no ketiv/qere note falls in this chapter, so nothing is owed. Two blemishes noted without displacing support: the unpointed three-token mention of the formation is labelled byte tier where it collates at skeleton, and the full pointed run of MT 8:10 is glossed only by 'for God is with us'.

items.claim: The rear seam cuts through a two-noun pairing that the bytes attest in only two verses in the whole book, and the row discloses no cross-seam cohesion at all; inside the span two distinct objects on one consonantal string go unnamed.
items.evidence: The row's own closing quote is צ֖וֹר תְּעוּדָ֑ה חֲת֥וֹם תּוֹרָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.8.16, byte tier). The very next unit opens לְתוֹרָ֖ה וְלִתְעוּדָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.8.20, byte tier) - the same two nouns, in reverse order. One of the pair stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses - MT 8:16 and MT 8:20) and the other in 5 (sweep: 5 verses), so the PAIRING of the two is unique to these two verses, it straddles this row's own rear seam at MT 8:18|8:19, and both witnesses render it. A byte-attested device straddling a row's own seam argues continuity against that seam unless it is disclosed, and this row's device note discloses only an internal uncertainty about where quoted divine speech yields to the prophet's voice - a byte-level fact bearing directly on the boundary it is drawing goes unmentioned. Second defect, same lens: the row refers to the sanctuary-and-stumbling-stone judgment in English only, while the span's bytes carry וּלְצ֨וּר מִכְשׁ֜וֹל (oshb:Isa.8.14, byte tier) two verses before the differently-pointed token that opens MT 8:16 - two distinct objects on one contiguous consonantal string (sweep: 23 verses carry that string book-wide, a contained-substring class that blends objects), neither of them named. Third, minor: the front-seam frame is quoted honestly at byte tier and its ownership is correctly divine, but the run begins כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה (oshb:Isa.8.11, byte tier) - a subordinating particle binding back across the seam the row asks it to open - and the row calls it a fresh onset without noting that. Parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 8:15 and MT 8:18 inside the span, SAMEKH at MT 8:10 at the front seam; tier-3, single-witness); no ketiv/qere note falls in this chapter.

items.claim: Neither seam is argued from the bytes: the front cut ignores the two-noun pairing its own second verse inherits from three verses back across that seam, and the rear cut is justified by the row's administrative range rather than by the text, with the one cross-seam signal it does disclose reduced to tone.
items.evidence: The unit's second verse opens לְתוֹרָ֖ה וְלִתְעוּדָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.8.20, byte tier), the reversed twin of צ֖וֹר תְּעוּדָ֑ה חֲת֥וֹם תּוֹרָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.8.16, byte tier) three verses back on the far side of the front seam; one of the paired nouns stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses), both of them here, so a byte-level fact bearing directly on this seam is a cohesion signal the row never mentions - its front-seam argument is purely topical. For the rear boundary the row states only that MT 8:22 is the last verse of an assigned range: that is administration, not evidence, and it also puts range-administration language into the row's prose. What the bytes do show at that seam is held rather than assertable: MT 8:22 closes מְע֣וּף צוּקָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.8.22, byte tier) and the adjoining verse opens כִּ֣י לֹ֣א מוּעָף֮ לַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מוּצָ֣ק (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1, byte tier) - the same consonant sets in different vocalic patterns, which the staged extract cannot confirm as one root because it carries no morphology layer, though both witnesses render the pair alike; the two forms are NOT a contiguous consonantal match, so no sweep digit supports them and no verbatim label may be attached. The row's disclosure calls that seam only a tonal reversal. Verified in the row's favour: the zone-A dual-cite at the rear seam is written correctly (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1) and lands on the right content, the Zebulun/Naphtali line; parashah disclosure is right - no parashah mark falls inside MT 8:19-8:22 (0 marks over those 4 verses) and the SAMEKH at MT 8:18 at the front seam is named (tier-3, single-witness, and its absence inside the span carries no weight either way); no ketiv/qere note falls in this chapter or at the zone edge.
